original_text: Upon completion, the document will act as a binding contract between developers and users and will provide a common point of reference for system expectations.

attribute_scores.rationale: The intent is clear as a meta-statement about the document, but it lacks precision regarding who the specific 'users' are.
As a system requirement, it lacks all necessary operational conditions, inputs, triggers, and expected behaviors.
While not directly conflicting with domain logic, it is inconsistent with the nature of a technical system requirement.
It completely fails to follow standard requirement syntax (<Condition> The <System> shall <Action>) and lacks the mandatory modal verb 'shall'.
Factually, an SRS often serves these contractual purposes, but placing this statement as a formal 'Functional' requirement inside the SRS specification is incorrect.
It combines two distinct concepts: acting as a binding contract and providing a common point of reference.
It is virtually impossible to objectively test or verify this statement as a software system requirement.

shortcomings.problematic_excerpt: Upon completion, the document will act as...
shortcomings.explanation: The statement violates IEEE 830 and ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 standards for requirement structure by failing to use the mandatory modal verb 'shall' and omitting the system subject and action.

shortcomings.problematic_excerpt: act as a binding contract between developers and users and will provide a common point of reference for system expectations.
shortcomings.explanation: The statement combines multiple independent clauses with 'and', merging the contractual administrative function with the reference documentation function.
This is a descriptive meta-statement about the document's legal/project management status rather than a testable software system requirement, making verification impossible.

layer1.document_understanding_summary: This statement describes the purpose and administrative role of the Software Requirements Specification (SRS) document itself within the EVLA backend system development context, rather than specifying an actual functional capability, behavior, or constraint of the radio astronomy correlator backend software.

layer2.reasoning_summary: All candidate defects are confirmed as genuine architectural and requirements engineering shortcomings because REQ-be_srs-001 is written as a meta-statement about the SRS document itself rather than a verifiable technical requirement for the radio astronomy correlator backend signal processing system.

layer3.original_text: Upon completion, the document will act as a binding contract between developers and users and will provide a common point of reference for system expectations.
layer3.refined_text: The EVLA backend system shall provide a documented specification of system expectations for reference by developers and users.
changes_made: Replaced the descriptive meta-statement and administrative clauses with the mandatory subject and modal verb 'The EVLA backend system shall'.
Removed compound clauses ('act as a binding contract ... and will provide') to ensure singularity and verifiability.
Restructured the requirement into standard EARS ubiquitous format focusing on the verifiable system capability.
layer3.functional_intent_preservation_rationale: The refined requirement maintains the core intent that the backend system capabilities and expectations are explicitly documented and accessible as a reference point for both developers and users, while translating a non-testable project management statement into a verifiable system requirement.

checks.observations: The refinement successfully replaced the non-compliant sentence structure with a 'shall' statement containing a system subject.
No new vague or subjective terms were added.

The requirement states that the system itself shall provide a documented specification of system expectations. This is factually incorrect and represents an unwarranted assumption: a backend signal processing software system does not generate or provide its own Software Requirements Specification (SRS) document at runtime as a system feature.

The original text was a preamble/administrative statement about the SRS document itself. Transforming this meta-statement into a runtime software requirement ('The EVLA backend system shall provide a documented specification...') fundamentally distorts the intent by misattributing document management functions to the software runtime domain.
Grammatically, the sentence uses 'shall' and follows standard requirements structure, but it fails domain-context validity.

unwarranted_assumptions_detected: Assumes the backend software system is responsible for providing its own specification document as a functional capability.
layer4.critique_and_feedback: While the Layer 3 refiner successfully addressed the syntactic defects of the original meta-statement by introducing a 'shall' structure, the resulting requirement is conceptually flawed. The original text (REQ-be_srs-001) is clearly a document preamble or administrative metadata describing the purpose of the SRS document, not a functional requirement of the EVLA backend signal processing system. Forcing a document administrative statement into a software system requirement ('The EVLA backend system shall provide a documented specification...') invents a nonsensical software capability. Document metadata and contractual statements of the SRS document should be handled as introductory documentation artifacts rather than forced into the system requirements list.
